caseno: Criminal Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 198 of 1995
lawyer:
Dr. Kamal Hossain, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Kazi Shahabuddin Ahmed, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner
Mr. K.S. Nabi, Attorney General, (Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, Assistant Attorney General with him) instructed by Mvi. Md. Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Dr. Taslima Nasreen ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Mohammad Nurul Alam, Officer-in-Charge and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
A.T.M. Afzal, C.J: This petition, at the instance of the accused-petitioner, arises out of a proceeding under section 295A of the Penal Code, Complaint Case No. 1315 of 1994, initiated by the Officer-in-Charge, Motijheel police station on 4.6.1994 being authorised by the Government under section 196 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, briefly the Code, which is pending before the Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 3. The learned Magistrate took cognizance on the same day and issued warrant of arrest. The accused-petitioner surrendered before the High Court Division and was granted bail. After charge was framed on 5.11.94., the petitioner moved the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code for quashing of the proceeding, Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 197 of 1995, on the ground that there was no sanction from the Government as regard under section 188 of the Code. The Rule issued in that case was, however, discharged holding that a sanction under section 188 might be obtained before starting the trial. The Government then accorded sanction by a letter dated 1.4.95. 

 5. It appears that the same arguments assailing the sanction order were made in the High Court Division and the learned Judges labouriously considered them and by a longer judgment rejected the contentions holding that there was no illegality in the sanction order. The rule was discharged by the impugned judgment and order dated 1.8.95 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1790 of 1995. Now this petition for leave to appeal from the same. 

 6. This petition came up for hearing about a year ago and after hearing Dr. Kamal Hossain, learned Counsel for the petitioner, then, we indicated that the whole exercise done by the Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate upto the High Court Division as to the validity of the sanction order was both unfortunate and uncalled for as the prosecution is yet to prove the sanction order in the trial (which has not yet begun) and has not got the opportunity to bring the evidence on record to meet the objections as are or may be raised regarding the validity of the sanction. It was like putting the cart before the horse. We were about to dismiss the petition with this observation. Dr. Kamal Hossain then suggested that since it was a sensitive case having religion political content and the political atmosphere outside was not also congenial, it may serve the ends of Justice if the matter is kept pending here for some time instead of allowing the trial to begin in that volatile situation. We agreed to his suggestion and thereafter granted repeated adjournments on his prayer. Lately we were told that since there was a change in the Government and as a new Attorney General had assumed office, there may be a change in the government policy in respect of the present case and we may not have to send the case back for trial. We again adjourned the case a number of times on such prayer and wanted to hear the learned Attorney General if he had any clear instruction from the government in the matter. 

 8. We indicated a year before what in our opinion was best but deferred the order in the hope which we were induced to entertain by making repeated prayers for adjournment submitting that a change in the policy of the government so far as this case is concerned was round the corner. 

 9. Now that the learned Attorney General has not come up with any clear submission, there is no reason to keep the matter pending any longer. As regards the present prayer of the petitioner for an order of remand to the High Court Division, it will be sufficient to observe that the grounds urged for such an order only vindicate the view we had already expressed that the validity of the sanction order can only be agitated and considered after the prosecution got an opportunity to place the facts by way of leading evidence to meet the objections that are to be or may be raised. Law prescribes a procedure for scrutiny of evidence that may be adduced in a trail. The High Court Division does not embark upon 2 assessing any part of such evidence or materials either under section 561A or in the name of Judicial review nor can ask the prosecution to lead evidence by affidavit in support of any fact upon which the prosecution case rests or may rest. It is fundamental to the rule of law that the procedural law as to holding of a trial must not be interfered with. 

 10. We have noticed that the government lawyer produced some photo copies of note sheets from government file in answer to the objections raised by the petitioner and the learned Magistrate relied on them. The learned Magistrate should have realised that the Government must get an opportunity to adduce proper evidence before he could decide on the objections raised. The objections are legal but they are founded on facts or in their absence. In any case, it is for the trial court to form its own opinion after the parties have led evidence. The High Court Division will not superimpose itself in that ordinary and usual process.
